roast.title: Pot Roast for One (Oven, Old Church Way)
ingredients: 1 medium potato, chunks (or 4-5 small red, whole)
1 cup beef broth (or water + bouillon cube)
Sprig thyme or pinch dried thyme
steps: Heat oven to 300°F.
Brown roast in oil, 3 min per side.
Sauté onion 2 min, add broth and coffee.
Return roast, add carrots, potato, thyme.
Cover, bake 2.5–3 hrs. Rest before serving.
roast.tip: Brown the roast well—it's where the flavor comes from.

gravy.title: Pan Gravy
steps: Mix flour and cold water until smooth.
Heat pot liquid on stove, medium.
Stir in slurry, bubble 2 minutes.
Taste and add salt if needed.
Serve hot over roast and vegetables.
gravy.tip: Always mix flour with cold water first—no lumps!

biscuit.title: Three Buttermilk Biscuits
steps: Heat oven to 425°F.
Mix dry ingredients, rub in cold butter.
Stir in buttermilk just until shaggy.
Pat, fold twice, cut 3 biscuits.
Bake 12–14 min until golden.
biscuit.tip: Fold the dough twice for tall, flaky biscuits.

peas.title: Creamed Peas
steps: Melt butter, stir in flour, cook 1 min.
Add milk gradually, stir until thick.
Add peas, salt, sugar.
Cook 2–3 min until hot and bright green.
Serve immediately.
peas.tip: Don't overcook peas—they'll go gray and mushy.

lettuce.title: Wilted Lettuce with Warm Bacon Dressing
steps: Put lettuce and onion in bowl.
Cook bacon pieces until crisp.
Stir sugar, vinegar, water into hot bacon fat.
Pour hot dressing over lettuce, toss.
Top with bacon pieces.
lettuce.tip: Pour the dressing on hot so the lettuce just wilts.

ham.title: Ham Steak with Fried Apples
steps: Brown ham steak, 3 min per side.
Remove ham, melt butter in skillet.
Cook apples 4 min, turning once.
Add brown sugar, cinnamon, cook 1 min.
Return ham, spoon apples and syrup over.
ham.tip: Ham is already cooked—just brown for flavor.

crisp.title: Apple Crisp for One
steps: Heat oven to 375°F.
Toss apple with sugar, cinnamon in dish.
Mix oats, flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, salt.
Cut in butter, sprinkle over apples.
Bake 25–30 min until bubbly and brown.
crisp.tip: A tart apple works best for crisp flavor.

hash.title: Roast Beef Hash (Monday)
ingredients: 1 cup leftover potato and carrot, chopped
steps: Cook onion in butter 3 min.
Add potato, carrot, press flat, brown 4 min.
Turn, add beef, press, brown 4 min.
Stir in gravy at end.
Crack egg in well, cover, cook 3–4 min.
hash.tip: Leave hash alone to get a crisp bottom.

noodles.title: Beef and Noodles (Tuesday)
steps: Boil broth and gravy in small pot.
Add noodles, cook 8–9 min, stirring.
Stir in beef to warm.
Serve over mashed potatoes if you like.
noodles.tip: Cook noodles right in the broth for flavor.

pudding.title: Bread Pudding for One
ingredients: 1 day-old biscuit or thick bread slice, torn
steps: Heat oven to 350°F, butter ramekin.
Put bread and raisins in ramekin.
Beat egg, milk, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla.
Pour over bread, soak 10 min.
Bake 25 min until puffed, center set.
pudding.tip: Let bread soak before baking for best texture.

hotbeef.title: Hot Beef Sandwich
steps: Warm beef in gravy, covered, until steaming.
Place bread on plate.
Lay beef on bread, potatoes beside.
Pour gravy over everything.
Eat with knife and fork.
hotbeef.tip: Warm beef in gravy so it stays moist.

chicken.title: Poor Man's Sunday Chicken Dinner (Leg Quarter)
steps: Heat oven to 350°F.
Brown chicken skin side down 5 min.
Add onion, carrot, potato, pour broth around.
Sprinkle thyme, bake uncovered 1 hour.
Check chicken is 165°F by bone.
chicken.tip: Pour broth around, not over, to keep skin crisp.
